Appendix A: The appendix supplies smooth maps on manifolds with corners, extension lemmas, and a concrete smooth-function construction
Introduction: The introduction frames symplectic topology as a subject born from mechanics and sharpened by global rigidity, fixed point, and embedding phenomena
Chapter 1: The chapter moves from variational mechanics to Hamiltonian vector fields, symplectomorphisms, Poisson brackets, and the first global problems
Chapter 2: The chapter builds the standard matrix model, symplectic linear group, Lagrangian planes, compatible complex structures, bundles, and first Chern class
Chapter 3: The chapter defines symplectic manifolds, proves normal-form principles, organizes submanifolds, and introduces contact structures
Chapter 4: The chapter explains almost complex structures, integrability, Kahler examples, surfaces, and the first J-holomorphic curve viewpoint
Chapter 5: The chapter studies symplectic group actions, moment maps, quotients, convexity, localization, and links to geometric invariant theory
Chapter 6: The chapter develops symplectic fibrations, symplectic connections, Hamiltonian holonomy, coupling forms, and Hamiltonian fibrations
Chapter 7: The chapter constructs symplectic manifolds through blow-ups, connected sums, telescope constructions, and Donaldson submanifolds
Chapter 8: The chapter treats periodic orbits, the Poincare-Birkhoff theorem, and billiards as concrete two-dimensional symplectic dynamics
Chapter 9: The chapter connects generating functions, symplectic action, discrete Hamiltonian mechanics, Hamiltonian symplectomorphisms, and Lagrangian graphs
Chapter 10: The chapter studies the symplectomorphism group, Hamiltonian subgroup, flux homomorphism, Calabi homomorphism, and topology of these groups
Chapter 11: The chapter develops the Arnold conjecture, fixed points, Morse and Conley tools, Lagrangian intersections, and a first Floer homology overview
Chapter 12: The chapter treats nonsqueezing, rigidity, Hofer geometry, Hofer-Zehnder capacity, and a variational proof of capacities
Chapter 13: The chapter surveys symplectic existence and uniqueness, examples, Taubes-Seiberg-Witten theory, and symplectic four-manifolds

Chapter 14: The chapter lists open questions across structures, symplectomorphisms, Lagrangians, Fano manifolds, Donaldson hypersurfaces, contact geometry, continuous symplectic topology, embeddings, and Euclidean space
